title: Problem Overview: Optimal Convergence Rate
content: This file addresses the open question of optimal convergence rates for arctangent-based $\pi$ series. The Leibniz series $\pi/4 = 1 - 1/3 + 1/5 - \cdots$ is the simplest such series but converges agonizingly slowly at rate $\Theta(1/N)$. Machin-type formulas evaluate arctangent at smaller arguments to achieve exponential convergence. The formalization proves both the $O(1/N)$ upper bound and its sharpness.

title: Partial Sum Definition and Convergence
content: Defines the $n$-th partial sum $S(n) = \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} (-1)^i/(2i+1)$ and immediately establishes convergence to $\pi/4$ via Mathlib's `Real.tendsto_sum_pi_div_four`. This Mathlib result encodes the classical identity $\arctan(1) = \pi/4$ combined with the Taylor series expansion of arctangent at $x = 1$.

title: Step Formula and Sign Lemmas
content: Three helper results: (1) `S_step` gives $S(n+1) - S(n) = (-1)^n/(2n+1)$, the telescoping identity. (2) `neg_one_pow_even` shows $(-1)^{2k} = 1$. (3) `neg_one_pow_odd` shows $(-1)^{2k+1} = -1$. These decompose the sign pattern into even/odd cases, which is the foundation of the monotonicity argument.

title: Even Partial Sums Are Monotonically Increasing
content: Proves $S(2k) \leq S(2(k+1))$ using `monotone_nat_of_le_succ`. The key calculation: $S(2k+2) - S(2k) = S(2k+1) - S(2k) + S(2k+2) - S(2k+1) = 1/(4k+1) - 1/(4k+3) > 0$ since $4k+1 < 4k+3$. The proof uses `div_le_div_of_nonneg_left` to compare the reciprocals.

title: Odd Partial Sums Are Antitone (Decreasing)
content: Proves $S(2(k+1)+1) \leq S(2k+1)$ using `antitone_nat_of_succ_le`. The calculation mirrors the even case: $S(2k+3) - S(2k+1) = -1/(4k+3) + 1/(4k+5) = -2/((4k+3)(4k+5)) < 0$. Together with even monotonicity, this establishes the interlacing property of the alternating series.

title: Sandwich Property: S(2k) ≤ π/4 ≤ S(2k+1)
content: The limit $\pi/4$ is trapped between the monotone even subsequence (below) and the antitone odd subsequence (above). The proofs use `ge_of_tendsto` and `le_of_tendsto` with `eventually_atTop`: since $S(2k)$ is increasing and converges to $\pi/4$, every value $S(2k)$ is at most $\pi/4$. The symmetric argument applies to odd partial sums.

title: Error Bound: |π/4 - S(n)| ≤ 1/(2n+1)
content: The **main result**: the alternating series estimation theorem for the Leibniz series. The proof splits into even and odd cases. For even $n = 2k$: $0 \leq \pi/4 - S(2k) \leq S(2k+1) - S(2k) = 1/(4k+1) = 1/(2n+1)$. For odd $n = 2k+1$: $S(2k+1) - \pi/4 \leq S(2k+1) - S(2k+2) = 1/(4k+3) = 1/(2n+1)$. The case split uses `Nat.even_or_odd`.

title: Rate Sharpness: |S(n+1) - S(n)| = 1/(2n+1)
content: Proves the $O(1/N)$ rate is **tight**: consecutive partial sums differ by exactly $1/(2n+1)$. Since $|\pi/4 - S_n|$ is bounded below by half the gap between consecutive sums (in the limit), this shows no better rate is achievable. The proof uses `abs_div`, `abs_pow`, and `abs_neg` to simplify $|(-1)^n/(2n+1)| = 1/(2n+1)$.
